Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · Time, the calendar & feasts

party noun

a celebration

also parties, throw a party, have a party, get-together, celebration, celebrations, give a party

classical

Cic. Sen. 45: accubitiōnem epulārem amīcōrum … convīvium nōmināvērunt
Traupman 114, 128

convīvium, convīviī n.

noun, second declension

a party; friends eating and drinking together

A “living together”, as Cicero explains the word (Sen. 45). Traupman’s word for a party: convīvium agitāre, to throw a party (pp. 114, 128; cf. Plaut. Mil. 2.2.10, Lewis & Short: domī agitāre).

Other words

  • cōmissātiō, cōmissātiōnis f. — a revel, drinking and merrymaking after dinner

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Mur. 13 (Lewis & Short); Liv. 40.13.3 (Lewis & Short)

    Greek κῶμος: the noisy round of the houses after dinner. Not for a children’s party.

  • circulus, circulī m. — a gathering, a circle of friends

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.56: circulōs aliquōs et sessiunculās (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. party, get-together

    People gathered to talk, often named beside convīvia (Cic. Balb. 57, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • frīgoribus partō agricolae plērumque fruuntur mūtuaque inter sē laetī convīvia cūrant. invītat geniālis hiems cūrāsque resolvit

    in the cold, farmers mostly enjoy what they have earned, and happily give parties for one another; festive winter invites them and loosens their caresVerg. G. 1.300–302

  • Agitābō convīvium prō eō.

    I’m going to throw a party for him.Traupman 128

  • convīvium dare

    to give a partyTraupman 356

  • convīvium agitāre

    to throw a partyTraupman 356

See also birthday party, dinner party, banquet.
